exposure: Mode of delivery (normal vaginal delivery, assisted vaginal delivery, planned cesarean section, emergency cesarean section)
outcome: Body mass index at age 17 years
Body fat percentage at age 17 years
cohort: 8,880 mother-child pairs from the United Kingdom Millennium Cohort Study
finding: This large longitudinal study did not find an association between cesarean section or induction of labour and overweight, obesity, or body fat percentage in adolescents.
mod_finding: Adolescents born by cesarean section did not have an elevated BMI or body fat percentage compared to those born by normal vaginal delivery.
